subject: Business Models
title: Cable TV's Bundle
description: Learn Cable TV's Bundle in one minute.

hook.text: Cable TV charged $50-$150/month for 500 channels. Nobody watched more than 20.

buildup.text: The cable bundle locked Americans into long contracts with early termination fees and price increases.

discovery.text: Cable companies realized subscribers didn't cancel over small price hikes. Annual 5-8% increases became routine.

twist.text: Netflix launched streaming for $8/month. Cord-cutting began. Cable lost 25 million subscribers by 2023.

climax.text: Cable showed that subscription pricing power is enormous—until a better alternative appears.

punchline.text: 500 channels, 20 watched. Cable proved bundles can overcharge for decades.

quiz.question: What triggered the decline of cable TV subscriptions?

details.summary: Cable television's subscription bundle charged consumers monthly fees for access to hundreds of channels, creating a multi-billion dollar industry at its peak..
details.whyItMatters: Cable TV's rise and fall demonstrates both the power and the limits of subscription bundling. The model extracted maximum revenue for decades before customer resentment and streaming competition triggered massive cord-cutting that continues today.
takeaways: Bundling maximized total revenue by subsidizing niche channels with popular ones
Average cable bills exceeded $100 monthly at the model's peak
Cord-cutting accelerated as streaming offered unbundled alternatives

faq.question: Why was cable bundling profitable for so long despite customer complaints?
faq.answer: There were no viable alternatives for live TV and premium content. Content companies required carriage of multiple channels as a package deal. High switching costs and infrastructure monopolies in local markets gave subscribers few choices. The bundle was mandatory, not optional.

faq.question: How has the streaming era changed subscription bundling?
faq.answer: Consumers now subscribe to individual streaming services instead of one cable bundle. Ironically, as streaming services multiply, total subscription costs can exceed old cable bills. This has led to re-bundling through offerings like Disney's bundle and Apple One.
